summary: Introduction, development, an unexpected turn, and a reconciliation that makes sense of it. Driven by contrast and discovery rather than conflict.
_lineage: A traditional East Asian four-part structure (Chinese qǐ chéng zhuǎn hé; Japanese kishōtenketsu), common in classical poetry, four-panel comics and short fiction. It needs no antagonist: the turn does the work.

beats.name: Introduction (ki)
beats.describe: The people and the place, in their own rhythm. Nothing has to be wrong yet.
lookFor: a calm establishing of who and where

beats.name: Development (shō)
beats.describe: The situation deepens. The reader understands the world better and comes to care about it.
lookFor: the same thread followed further, with more detail and feeling

beats.name: The turn (ten)
beats.describe: Something unexpected arrives, often unrelated at first, and recasts everything before it.
lookFor: a new element that seems to come from elsewhere

beats.name: Reconciliation (ketsu)
beats.describe: The parts come together in a new understanding. The ending joins the turn to the beginning.
lookFor: a final image or insight that links the turn to the start
